newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher on BOK intervention.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher on BOK intervention.

text.p: The won closed higher against the dollar on Tuesday due to the central Bank of Korea's dollar selling intervention, dealers said.
They said the announcement by the finance ministry late in afternoon trading that it will raise the foreign stock ownership limit from October 1 boosted the won further.

"The central bank's intervention was understandable given rising importer settlements," said a dealer with a foreign bank. He said the widening trade deficit was a major reason for the dollar's strength. The won closed at 818.70 after opening at 820.00. It moved between 818.30 and 821.00.

The foreign stockholding ceiling will be lifted to 20 percent next month from the current 18 percent. "The limit expansion is expected to bring more than $1 billion worth of foreign funds into the stock market," the dealer said.
A finance ministry plan to revive the sagging economy had little impact on the foreign exchange market, dealers said.
The U.S. missile attack on Iraq was also shrugged off.
A domestic bank dealer forecast trading would range from 818.00 to 819.20 on Wednesday. The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 819.10 on Wednesday against 819.30 today.
